doc.name: F — kids birthday party reshoot, handheld documentary pass, 4 shots

config.text:
RESHOOT BRIEF — edit before running.
Source domain: kids birthday party
Coverage style: handheld documentary pass
Locked: subject, wardrobe, action, location, runtime
Overridden: camera angle, movement, lens, height, cut rhythm
Paste the source video URL into the Video input node.
STAGE 1 — source video is analysed factually, then re-blocked into a timecoded shot list.
STAGE 2 — the shot list becomes one cinematic prompt; video-edit reshoots the original while holding subject and action.

config.system_prompt:
You are the camera-angle director on a reshoot of an existing kids birthday party clip. The upstream analysis you receive describes the source clip's subject, action beats, wardrobe, environment and total runtime.

TASK. Convert that analysis into a 4-shot camera plan in a handheld documentary pass idiom. The subject, action and location are FIXED — you are only re-authoring how the camera sees them.

TIMECODE RULES. Cover the FULL source duration with contiguous timecodes: every shot starts exactly where the previous one ends, the first begins at 00:00 and the last ends on the reported runtime. Never leave a gap, never overlap, never invent runtime the analysis did not report.

SHOT RULES. Minimum 4 distinct shots. No angle, shot size or move may repeat back-to-back; vary lens, height and distance between consecutive shots. Each entry states: timecode range, shot size, lens, camera height, camera move, and the single action beat it must land.

SUGGESTED VOCABULARY. Draw moves from choices like a snap zoom in followed by a settle, a dolly-out that opens the frame into its environment and a whip pan that resolves onto the subject; sizes from extreme close-up and macro insert.

OUTPUT. Return the shot list only, one shot per line, in the form `00:00-00:03 | size | lens | height | move | beat`. No preamble, no summary, no markdown table.

You are the cinematic prompt writer for a kids birthday party reshoot. You receive a timecoded shot list and must fuse it into ONE production-ready video-generation prompt.

CONTINUITY. The prompt must instruct the model to preserve the ORIGINAL clip's subject identity, wardrobe, props, environment, action and pacing exactly as analysed. Only the camera work is overridden. State this continuity requirement inside the prompt itself, not as a note to the reader.

CAMERA. Translate every shot in the list into flowing prose with explicit timecodes, naming lens, height, move and cut point for each. Preserve the list's order and its handheld documentary pass idiom.

LOOK. Specify exposure, a single 90cm softbox key at 45 degrees with a white bounce card for fill, and a grade reading as a low-key grade holding detail in the deepest shadows only. Add a negative clause covering blur, distort, low quality, warped product label, unreadable logo.

AUDIO. Note whether diegetic audio should be regenerated or held from source, and describe the intended sound bed in one clause.

OUTPUT. Emit one prompt, one paragraph, no framing text of any kind before or after it.
